findings.title: Task 20's enumerated call-site list misses a guide-file read in `phaseShorthand.ts`, and the `prompt.ts` wiring point is ordered after an earlier guide read
findings.description:
Task 20 instructs grepping for `PROMPT_FILE_RELATIVE_PATH` and then presents an exhaustive-looking list: `build.ts` (~78), `prompt.ts` (~60 and ~116), `setup-ide.ts`. The grep actually hits `packages/cli/src/utils/phaseShorthand.ts:3` and `:22`, which reads `path.join(projectPath, PROMPT_FILE_RELATIVE_PATH)` — and that constant (`packages/core/src/services/constants.ts:7`) resolves to `project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides/prompt.ai-project.system.md`, i.e. a read of guide content. Two concrete consequences on the #80 state (fresh clone, empty guide dir):
- `cf prompt get P1` calls `resolvePhaseInput()` at `packages/cli/src/commands/prompt.ts:114` (which reads the guide file via `getPhaseShorthands()` for shorthand input) **before** the task's stated wiring point at line 116. If `ensureGuideReady` is inserted at "~line 116" as specified, the shorthand path throws ENOENT before auto-init can run.
- `cf prompt list` reads the guide file at line 62 via `getAllPrompts()` and again at line 65; a junior AI placing the call exactly at the enumerated "line 60" works only by luck of proximity.

This leaves unmeasured the design's D3/Scope requirement that `ensureCheckout()` be "called from every CLI command and MCP tool that reads guide content," and the success criterion that a freshly cloned project's commands succeed. Fix: name `phaseShorthand.ts` explicitly (or state the wiring must precede `resolvePhaseInput()` and `getPhaseShorthands()` in `prompt.ts`), and phrase the enumeration as "all hits, including but not limited to" since Task 20 already mandates the grep.

findings.title: Task 22 specifies a wiring point that cannot deliver the `notices` array it requires
findings.description: Task 22 says to call `ensureCheckout()` "before `createContextPipeline` (~line 57)" and "before `resolvePromptFilePath` (~line 98)" and append `message` to a `notices: string[]` on the tool result. But line 57 sits inside the shared helper `generateContext()` (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:26`), whose signature is `Promise<string>` — there is no tool result in scope there, and changing its return type ripples into `context_build` **and** `template_preview` (line 220), which the task never mentions. Meanwhile lines 98/249/282 are inside `resolvePromptFileForTools()`/the `prompt_list`/`prompt_get` handlers, which return `jsonResult()`/`textResult()` objects — a different shape each. The success criterion ("`grep -rn "notices"` shows one shared shape, not per-tool ad hoc fields") is unachievable without a decision the task does not make: where notices are captured, whether `generateContext` returns `{ context, notices }`, and whether `template_preview` emits a notice. State these in Task 22 (or split the plumbing sub-step out) so the task is independently completable.

findings.title: Commit markers are inline in checkbox items rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The required format is `**Commit**:` on a plain line, never a checkbox item. This file embeds "Commit: `…`" at the end of the final success-criteria bullet of each commit-bearing task (lines 100, 127, 153, 204, 224, 246, 276, 312, 333, 342, 373, 389, 412, and the final one in Task 32). Placement itself is good — markers sit after tested points and are distributed across all five parts, not bunched at the end — but the markers are neither bolded nor on their own plain lines, so any tooling or reviewer scanning for `**Commit**:` lines will find none. Restate each as a plain `**Commit**: <message>` line immediately after (not inside) its task's checkbox list.

findings.title: Task 10's success criterion cannot be verified until Task 11 completes
findings.description: "Success criteria: typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field" makes Task 10 independently un-completable as written — its own green bar is defined in terms of a later task. (If `GuideInfo.checkout` is added as a required non-optional field, typecheck genuinely breaks between Task 10 and Task 11.) Either make the criterion self-contained ("typecheck passes; `checkout` is optional/null-initialized until Task 11") or merge Tasks 10 and 11 into one task.

findings.title: Success-criterion coverage is complete
findings.description: Cross-referenced all ten functional and four technical success criteria: fresh-clone `cf build` + stderr notice (Tasks 9/11/17/19/20/21), `--json` purity (21), read-only `Checkout: not initialized` (11/24), out-of-sync warning (17/18/21), `--strategy manual` + `Method: tarball` output (1/3/7/8), config-file alias (5/6), `cf init --strategy` with no `.gitmodules` (26/27), both `--help` outputs (25/27), managed-directory line + README section (28/29/30), malformed-config failure (6c), real-git fixtures and branch coverage (9/12/16/18/21/23), the two grep invariants (3/32), no commentless `catch` in `GuideManager.ts` (5/32), CHANGELOG/DEVLOG/README (30/31), and the verification walkthrough (32). No untraced scope creep found; no NFR is restated (F006 confirms), so no load-test or CI-gating task is required. Task count (32) and per-task effort (1–3) are proportionate to a three-issue slice, test tasks follow implementation tasks throughout, and there are no circular dependencies.
